findings.title: Error events zipped against nodestore result dict values by position
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids` and calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi`. It then pairs the results with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, which assumes the returned dict has one entry per requested id, in request order. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id, and backends do not guarantee that order or that missing keys are present. When they differ, error titles and messages get attached to the wrong event IDs, or entries are silently dropped. Look up each result with `events.get(node_id)` instead of relying on position.

findings.title: Error timestamps (seconds) compared with rrweb event timestamps (milliseconds)
findings.body: `gen_request_data` interleaves errors with recording events by comparing `error['timestamp']` to `event.get('timestamp')`. The error timestamp comes from nodestore event data and is in seconds since epoch. Top-level rrweb recording-segment event timestamps are in milliseconds. In real data every error therefore sorts before every breadcrumb, so the chronological ordering sent to Seer is wrong. The tests use seconds for both values and do not catch this. Normalize both values to the same unit before comparing.

findings.title: Migrations turned into no-ops that point to a migration not in this PR
findings.body: Both 0917 and 0920 now just return, with comments directing readers to `0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py`. That migration is not added in this change. If it does not already exist, organization saved searches are never converted to GroupSearchViews. Environments that already ran the original 0917 also keep its (allegedly erroneous) results with no corrective migration. The comment that the migration 'was never run' may also be inaccurate, since 0917 shipped with a test and was post-deployment. Add 0921 in this PR or fix the reference.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion check uses truthiness
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` use `self.initial_data.get("age")` and `.get("timestamp")` as truthy checks. A report with `age: 0` (common for fresh reports) and a timestamp therefore passes validation even though both fields are present. A report with neither field is also accepted, because both are `required=False`. Use `'age' in self.initial_data` and add an object-level `validate()` that requires exactly one of the two fields.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only filtered when a search query is present
findings.body: When `searchQuery` is empty, the memo returns `sorted` before the filter runs. As a result `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` stay visible in the default view and disappear only once the user types a search. Apply the hidden-attribute filter in both branches.

findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget renders hardcoded empty data
findings.body: With `use-table-widget-visualization` enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is given `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`, and `result.data`/`result.meta` are ignored. Every table widget for flagged orgs will render as an empty table. Pass the actual table results, or keep the flag off until the wiring is complete.

findings.title: 60s deadline for a batch of up to 100 external identity refreshes may break the reschedule chain
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` refreshes up to `chunk_size=100` identities, and each refresh makes a network call to the SSO provider. It reschedules `check_auth` only at the end of the task. With the new 60s processing deadline, a slow provider can get the task killed before that point. The self-rescheduling chain then stops, and further auth checks depend on the periodic trigger. Raise the deadline or reschedule before processing the batch.

findings.title: Per-issue recommended-event lookup when building PR comments
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` once per issue in the comment. Each call issues a Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch, so every comment build adds N sequential round trips. It also swallows all exceptions with only an info log. Consider fetching environments in bulk, or from group tag values.
